hints: Focus on oxidation numbers rather than the swapping of atoms, redox is only about a change in oxidation state.
Work out the oxidation state of xenon in both $\text{XeF}_6$ and $\text{XeO}_3$, remembering F is -1 and O is -2.
Check H, O and F as well, and if every element keeps the same number from left to right then no oxidation or reduction has happened.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a redox reaction**

Redox means oxidation numbers change. Oxidation is an increase in oxidation number, reduction is a decrease.

Rule to use:
$$\text{If no oxidation number changes, it is not redox}$$

**Assign oxidation states on the left**

In $\text{XeF}_6$, F is -1, so Xe must be +6 to balance 6 fluorines. In $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, H is +1 and O is -2. This is the normal pattern for these elements.

**Assign oxidation states on the right**

In $\text{XeO}_3$, O is -2, so $\text{Xe} + 3(-2) = 0$ gives Xe = +6. In $\text{HF}$, H is +1 and F is -1, just as usual.

**Compare and conclude**

Xe stays +6, H stays +1, O stays -2, F stays -1. Nothing is oxidised and nothing is reduced, so this is hydrolysis, not redox.

options.A: Incorrect. Hydrogen is +1 in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ on the left and +1 in $\text{HF}$ on the right. Reduction needs a decrease in oxidation number, which does not happen here.
options.B: Incorrect. Hydrogen stays at +1 throughout, so it is neither oxidised nor reduced. This option traps students who see H moving from O to F and assume electron transfer.
options.C: Incorrect. Xenon is +6 in $\text{XeF}_6$ and still +6 in $\text{XeO}_3$. Oxidation needs an increase in oxidation number, so xenon is not oxidised.
options.D: Correct. All oxidation numbers are unchanged: Xe +6 to +6, H +1 to +1, O -2 to -2, F -1 to -1. With no change in oxidation state, no redox occurs.
